MCP Security Scanner - Comprehensive security analysis for MCP servers

positional arguments:
  {static,remote,prompts,resources,instructions,virustotal,behavioral,pypi-scan,npm-scan,vulnerable-package,stdio,config,known-configs}
    static              Scan pre-generated MCP JSON files (offline/CI-CD mode)
    remote              Scan a remote MCP server (SSE or streamable HTTP)
    prompts             Scan prompts on an MCP server
    resources           Scan resources on an MCP server
    instructions        Scan server instructions on an MCP server
    virustotal          Scan files or directories for malware using VirusTotal
    behavioral          Scan MCP server source code for docstring/behavior
                        mismatches
    pypi-scan           Download and scan a PyPI package in a Docker sandbox
    npm-scan            Download and scan an npm package in a Docker sandbox
    vulnerable-package  Scan Python dependencies for known vulnerabilities
                        using pip-audit
    stdio               Scan an MCP server via stdio (local command execution)
    config              Scan all servers defined in a specific MCP config file
    known-configs       Scan all well-known MCP client config files on this
                        machine

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --api-key API_KEY     Cisco AI Defense API key (overrides
                        MCP_SCANNER_API_KEY environment variable)
  --endpoint-url ENDPOINT_URL
                        Cisco AI Defense endpoint URL (overrides
                        MCP_SCANNER_ENDPOINT environment variable)
  --llm-api-key LLM_API_KEY
                        LLM provider API key for LLM analysis (overrides
                        environment variable)
  --llm-timeout LLM_TIMEOUT
                        Timeout in seconds for LLM API calls (overrides
                        MCP_SCANNER_LLM_TIMEOUT environment variable)
  --stdio-timeout STDIO_TIMEOUT
                        Timeout in seconds for stdio server connections
                        (overrides MCP_SCANNER_STDIO_TIMEOUT environment
                        variable, default: 60)
  --analyzers ANALYZERS
                        Comma-separated list of analyzers to run. Options:
                        api, yara, llm, behavioral, virustotal, readiness,
                        vulnerable_package, meta (default: api,yara,llm)
  --enable-meta         Enable the LLM meta-analyzer for second-pass analysis.
                        Reviews findings from all other analyzers to filter
                        false positives, prioritize by actual risk, and
                        correlate related findings. Requires
                        MCP_SCANNER_LLM_API_KEY. Adds 'meta' to the analyzer
                        list.
  --output OUTPUT, -o OUTPUT
                        Save scan results to a file
  --verbose, -v         Print verbose output
  --log-level {debug,info,warning,error,critical}
                        Set log level for the mcpscanner library (overrides
                        --verbose). Useful for suppressing noisy output in
                        CI/CD pipelines.
  --detailed, -d        Show detailed results
  --raw, -r             Print raw JSON output to terminal
  --expand-vars {auto,linux,mac,windows,off}
                        Control env var expansion for stdio command/args. off:
                        no env expansion (only ~). linux/mac: expand $VAR and
                        ${VAR} (POSIX). windows: expand %VAR% (Windows style
                        only). auto: linux/mac on POSIX, windows on Windows.
  --server-url SERVER_URL
                        URL of the MCP server to scan (default:
                        https://mcp.deepwiki.com/mcp)
  --scan-known-configs  Scan all well-known MCP client config files on this
                        machine (windsurf, cursor, claude, vscode)
  --config-path CONFIG_PATH
                        Scan all servers defined in a specific MCP config file
                        (e.g., ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json)
  --stdio-command STDIO_COMMAND
                        Run a stdio-based MCP server using the given command
                        (e.g., 'uvx')
  --stdio-args STDIO_ARGS
                        Arguments passed to the stdio command (comma-
                        separated, e.g., '--from,mcp-server-fetch,mcp-server-
                        fetch')
  --stdio-arg STDIO_ARG
                        Repeatable single argument (e.g., --stdio-arg=--from
                        --stdio-arg=pkg). More reliable than --stdio-args for
                        complex package names.
  --stderr-file STDERR_FILE
                        Redirect server stderr to this file (useful for
                        debugging startup messages that may corrupt JSON
                        output)
  --stdio-env STDIO_ENV
                        Environment variables for the stdio server in
                        KEY=VALUE form; can be repeated
  --stdio-tool STDIO_TOOL
                        If provided, only scan this specific tool name on the
                        stdio server
  --bearer-token BEARER_TOKEN
                        Bearer token to use for remote MCP server
                        authentication (Authorization: Bearer <token>)
  --format {raw,summary,detailed,by_tool,by_analyzer,by_severity,table}
                        Output format (default: summary)
  --tool-filter TOOL_FILTER
                        Filter results by tool name (partial match)
  --analyzer-filter {api_analyzer,yara_analyzer,llm_analyzer,behavioral_analyzer,virustotal_analyzer,vulnerable_package_analyzer}
                        Filter results by specific analyzer
  --severity-filter {all,high,unknown,medium,low,safe}
                        Filter results by severity level (default: all)
  --hide-safe           Hide safe tools from output
  --stats               Show statistics about scan results
  --rules-path RULES_PATH
                        Path to directory containing custom YARA rules
  --source-path SOURCE_PATH
                        Path to MCP server source code file or directory
                        (required for behavioral analyzer)

Examples:
  # Live server scanning:
  mcp-scanner                                                    # Basic security scan with summary (all analyzers)
  mcp-scanner --api-key YOUR_API_KEY --endpoint-url <your-endpoint> # Scan with an endpoint
  mcp-scanner --format detailed --api-key YOUR_API_KEY         # Detailed security findings report with API
  mcp-scanner --format by_analyzer --llm-api-key YOUR_LLM_KEY  # Group findings by analysis engine with LLM
  mcp-scanner --format table --analyzers yara                  # YARA-only scanning with table format
  mcp-scanner --analyzers api,yara --severity-filter high      # API and YARA analysis, high severity only
  mcp-scanner --analyzer-filter llm_analyzer --stats           # Show only LLM analysis with statistics
  mcp-scanner --tool-filter "database" --output results.json  # Filter and save results to file
  mcp-scanner --analyzers llm --raw                            # LLM-only scan with raw JSON output
  mcp-scanner --analyzers api,llm --hide-safe                  # API and LLM scan, hide safe results
  mcp-scanner --scan-known-configs --expand-vars auto          # Scan configs with OS-appropriate expansion
  mcp-scanner --scan-known-configs --expand-vars linux/mac         # Expand $VAR and ${VAR} only (POSIX)
  mcp-scanner --scan-known-configs --expand-vars windows       # Expand %VAR% only (Windows style)

  # Static file scanning (CI/CD friendly):
  mcp-scanner static --tools tools.json --analyzers yara                         # Scan static tools file
  mcp-scanner static --prompts prompts.json --analyzers llm                     # Scan prompts file
  mcp-scanner static --resources resources.json --analyzers yara                # Scan resources file
  mcp-scanner static --tools t.json --prompts p.json --analyzers yara,llm,api   # Scan all three types
